resources.title: Bayes Theorem | Statement, Formula, Derivation, and Examples
resources.description: Gives the exact formula, a full derivation from conditional probability and the law of total probability, and worked examples for prior/posterior/likelihood terms that GATE DA numericals on Bayes' theorem directly test.

resources.title: Lec-48: Bayes Theorem & Total Probability with Examples
resources.description: A GATE-exam-focused walkthrough (published Jan 2024) that pairs the total probability theorem with Bayes' theorem and solves multiple exam-style numericals step by step, which is exactly the problem-solving skill GATE DA questions on this topic require.

resources.title: Pattern Recognition: Lecture 16 - Bayes Theorem
resources.description: An NPTEL lecture segment titled specifically "Bayes Theorem" (Mod-02 Lec-16 of the IIT Madras Pattern Recognition course) that derives the theorem rigorously and connects it to classification/decision-making, bridging pure probability into the ML applications GATE DA also tests.

resources.title: Continuous Probability Distributions (Uniform, Exponential, Normal — PDFs, mean, variance)
resources.description: Lays out, in one compact page, the exact PDF/mean/variance formulas for uniform, exponential, and normal distributions that GATE DA numericals directly test, with worked examples rather than generic probability theory.

resources.title: NOC: Probability Theory for Data Science — Week 3 (Poisson, Uniform, Exponential, Gamma, Normal distributions)
resources.description: This is the rare NPTEL course framed specifically for data science (not generic engineering probability), and its Week 3 module is dedicated entirely to Poisson, uniform, exponential, and normal distributions — the exact four listed in this GATE DA topic.

resources.title: Probability Ch3: Geometric, Binomial, Poisson, Uniform, Exponential, Normal Distributions
resources.instructor: Diana Lee (Santa Clara Univ., Amth108 course)
resources.description: A single focused lecture that walks through Poisson, uniform, exponential, and normal distributions back-to-back with derivations, which is useful for building the side-by-side intuition (PDF shape, memoryless property, when each applies) that GATE DA conceptual questions probe.

topic_name: Continuous Random Variables & Distributions (uniform, exponential, Poisson, normal)
subject: Probability & Statistics

resources.title: T-test: Types, Formulas & Worked Examples
resources.description: Walks through all three t-test variants (one-sample, independent two-sample, paired) with the exact test-statistic formulas, degrees-of-freedom, and numerical worked examples that GATE DA questions require you to compute by hand.

resources.title: Z-test: Formula, Types, Examples
resources.description: Derives the Z = (x̄ − μ)/(σ/√n) statistic and shows one-sample and two-sample z-test numericals, directly targeting the large-sample/known-variance scenario GATE DA distinguishes from the t-test.

resources.title: Inference for categorical data (chi-square tests) — unit
resources.description: A free, no-signup video-and-practice unit built specifically around chi-square goodness-of-fit and independence tests, giving the conceptual intuition plus step-by-step calculation of the χ² = Σ(O−E)²/E statistic that GATE DA's categorical-data questions test.

resources.title: Lecture 16: Projection Matrices and Least Squares (18.06 Linear Algebra)
resources.description: Strang derives the projection matrix P = A(A^T A)^-1 A^T from first principles and proves its defining idempotent (P^2=P) and symmetric (P^T=P) properties on the board, which is exactly the derivation GATE DA questions on projection/orthogonal-projection matrices are built around.

resources.title: Projection Matrix
resources.description: This write-up directly connects the three related special-matrix concepts in the topic (projection, idempotent P^2=P, and orthogonal projection when P is also symmetric) with worked numeric examples, making it a fast reference for exam-style property checks.

resources.title: Partition Matrix
resources.description: Covers the one sub-topic (partitioned/block matrices) not addressed by the projection-matrix resources above, with a worked 4x4 block decomposition and block-level addition/multiplication/inverse rules that mirror how GATE DA tests partitioned-matrix operations.

topic_name: Matrices and special matrix types (projection, orthogonal, idempotent, partition matrices)
subject: Linear Algebra

resources.title: Eigenvectors and eigenvalues | Essence of linear algebra, Chapter 14
resources.description: Builds the core geometric intuition for exactly this topic (why Av=λv means the vector's span doesn't rotate) that most GATE aspirants skip in favor of rote characteristic-polynomial mechanics, making the subsequent algebra (det(A-λI)=0, multiplicities) click conceptually rather than by memorization.

resources.title: Algebraic and Geometric Multiplicity
resources.description: Directly targets the exact GATE-testable sub-skill this topic emphasizes — computing the characteristic polynomial via det(A−λI) and then distinguishing algebraic vs. geometric multiplicity (with the key inequality geometric ≤ algebraic) — through five fully worked 2x2/3x3 examples, free with no signup.

resources.title: Mod-01 Lec-06: Method to Find Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors, Diagonalization of Matrices
resources.description: An NPTEL lecture segment that walks through the actual computational procedure GATE expects — finding eigenvalues/eigenvectors from the characteristic equation and then using them to diagonalize a matrix (A = PDP⁻¹) — rather than a generic full-course linear algebra lecture.

topic_name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors (incl. diagonalization, characteristic polynomial, algebraic vs geometric multiplicity)
subject: Linear Algebra

resources.title: Lecture 13: Introduction to Singular Value Decomposition (Part-1) | GO Classes Linear Algebra GATE DA

resources.title: Lecture 29: Singular Value Decomposition (18.06 Linear Algebra, Spring 2010)
resources.description: Gilbert Strang devotes this entire lecture to deriving SVD as the factorization A = U*Sigma*V^T that works for every matrix, giving the rigorous conceptual foundation (why U and V are orthogonal, why singular values are ordered) that GATE-level questions probe.

resources.title: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
resources.description: Provides a step-by-step worked numerical example computing U, Sigma, V for a small matrix by hand (via eigenvalues of A^T A), which directly mirrors the manual computation style GATE DA numerical-answer questions on SVD require, with no signup needed.

resources.title: Taylor series | Essence of calculus, chapter 11
resources.description: Builds the exact intuition GATE DA candidates need for this topic — why matching successive derivatives at a point produces an ever-better polynomial approximation of a function — through a visual, term-by-term construction rather than rote formula memorization.

resources.title: Taylor Series | Theorem, Proof, Formula & Applications in Engineering
resources.description: A GATE-oriented written explainer covering the Taylor/Maclaurin formula, proof, and derivations for sin(x), cos(x), e^x, plus five solved examples and a dedicated GATE CSE previous-year-questions section, making it directly exam-relevant for GATE DA's engineering mathematics syllabus.

resources.title: Lecture 05: Taylor Polynomial, Taylor Series (NPTEL Engineering Mathematics - I)

resources.title: Last Minute Notes (LMNs) - Python Programming
